proposal.falsifier: Falsified by any of the following, observed in a fresh episode executed from task entry on a frozen source set: (a) the fingerprint step shows that latch kind, source-segment structure, dt, shunt list and capacitance default are numerically identical to a prior episode AND a band freshly derived here contradicts a band carried from that episode, yet the carried band would have selected the delivering design (the precaution would then be provably unnecessary and its cost unjustified); (b) a design chosen by the discrete-grid predictor with all three logged margins positive and validated to within two dt ticks fails to deliver exactly one 8-byte frame by receive_deadline_s, while some legal design satisfying the same logged inequalities is observed to deliver (the selection rule is wrong); (c) after validation within two dt ticks, the predictor still misses the observed t_boot or t_done of the executed design by more than two dt ticks (the discrete formulation is still wrong, so revert to the base method and log the residuals); (d) a post-terminal event triggers a knob change, a new execution, or a changed diagnosis (the terminality rule is violated); (e) an achieved packet with the required bytes, a unique event id and time <= deadline is re-labelled a failure, or a budget/tool error is answered by re-sending an identical payload (discipline violated and cost paid twice); (f) the procedure changes two knobs in one execution, edits the task, physics, initial state, evaluator or budget, or reports the outcome as hardware validity, statistical advantage, migration, recursive self-improvement or external acceptance. Any (a)-(f) means the update is rejected in favour of base H, with the mismatch, the residuals and the executions actually spent recorded.
proposal.hypothesis: If H is consumed from task entry, then four changes each prevent a failure mode that is visible in the retained record rather than hypothetical. (1) Fingerprinting the acquired fields before any diagnosis prevents importing a design band from a sibling episode: the retained episodes share world id b-transient-behavior-v1 but differ in event_latch ('volatile' vs 'passive-mechanical'), in source structure (two segments 0-0.006 s at 16.667 mW plus 0.03-0.06 s at 3.667 mW with a shunt, vs a single segment 0-0.02 s at 7.5 mW) and in the capacitance default (1e-5 F vs 2.2e-5 F), so a band or floor remembered from one scenario is mis-specified in the other. (2) Terminality-first reading prevents diagnosing expected decay as failure: one retained trace already contains an 8-byte delivery at 0.0158 s followed by a brownout at 0.3395 s after the source segment ended, and reacting to it by lowering capacitance or raising the transmit floor moves in exactly the direction that produced zero frames in the other retained trace (capture at 0.0037-0.0079 s destroyed by an energy-threshold brownout at 0.0121 s). (3) Stating the predictor as discrete per-tick operations and matching it against a fingerprint-matched recorded trace before spending a candidate keeps forecast error inside two dt ticks; the retained closed form ceil((E_ready+boot_j)/charge_step) predicted 0.0166 s against an observed 0.0158 s, an eight-tick miss that was a formula defect, not a design defect. This is a procedural claim about method consumption under the frozen public model and public sources only; physical calibration is UNKNOWN and acceptance is external.
proposal.method_text:
H update v3: fingerprint -> terminality -> discrete predictor -> validated selection. Every statement is a prediction about consumption of the frozen public model and the acquired public sources. Physical calibration is UNKNOWN; acceptance is determined outside the participant. This artefact governs only how I order experiments, read observations and choose among designs. It is not a device assignment and it never edits the task, physics, initial state, event, source access, evaluator or budget.

STEP 0 (entry). Call inspect once. Record: service (application_bytes, event_time_s, receive_deadline_s, unique_valid_frames), legal_design_ranges, current_design, current_measurement, retained_failures, partition/scope, and the episode budget (candidate executions, distinct designs, tool_calls, requests, wall_seconds). Treat budget numbers as hard costs to be reported, not as targets to be used up.

STEP 1 (acquire and fingerprint). Acquire every listed source; record source_sha256 and the acquisition block (bytes, native_calls, new_scientific_executions, wall_seconds) as actual cost. Then write an explicit fingerprint of the fields that bound the design: event_latch kind, cap_initial_voltage_v, capacitance_f, ready_v, off_v, cap_voltage_max_v, boot_j, boot_delay_s, esr_ohm, output_v, tx_current_a, tx_duration_s, off_power_w, idle_power_w, harvest_efficiency, plus the whole source_segments list (start_s, end_s, power_w), dt_s, contact_duration_s, deadline_s and any shunts. RULE: no number, band, limit, or scenario conclusion computed in a previous episode is reused, even when the model id matches. Retained evidence that this rule is load-bearing: episodes recorded under the same model id differ in event_latch ('volatile' vs 'passive-mechanical'), in source structure (two segments 0-0.006 s at 16.667 mW and 0.03-0.06 s at 3.667 mW with a 40 uJ shunt at 0.012 s, versus one segment 0-0.02 s at 7.5 mW with no shunt), and in the capacitance default (1e-5 F vs 2.2e-5 F). Any band carried across would have been wrong. If a source or field is unavailable, record it as UNKNOWN together with which later rules become unavailable; never substitute a remembered value.

STEP 2 (terminality-first reading, before diagnosis). 2.1 Mark a delivery ACHIEVED iff a packet exists with application_bytes equal to service.application_bytes, one unique event id equal to the service event, and packet time <= receive_deadline_s. 2.2 Define the post-terminal region of a trace as all activity strictly after the last tx-complete (or after the last source-segment end when no transmission occurred). Post-terminal brownouts, spills, reboots and idles are expected decay: record them, do not diagnose them, and never let them justify a knob change or an execution. 2.3 Only an absent ACHIEVED packet, or an ACHIEVED packet that violates a service field, is a retained failure. Classify it as: (a) deadline miss; (b) no boot / never reached ready voltage; (c) brownout or reset before tx-complete (transient-transmission); (d) frame-shape violation (bytes, uniqueness, count, duplicates); (e) latch loss between capture and transmission. 2.4 Preserve failed checks, tool errors, unavailable actions and UNKNOWNs verbatim; never re-label a failure or an unknown as a success, and never let a later episode's outcome rewrite an earlier one.

STEP 3 (predictor stated on the recorded grid, before any execution is spent). Use the recorded dt_s and mirror the model's order of operations with discrete steps rather than a closed-form shortcut. Setup: e0 = 0.5*C*cap_initial_voltage_v^2. Per tick k at time t_k: input = (sum of segment power covering t_k)*harvest_efficiency; drain = off_power_w while not yet booted, else idle_power_w, plus tx_current_a*output_v while transmitting; e <- e + (input - drain)*dt, clamped at 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2 and floored at 0. Boot at the first k with e >= 0.5*C*ready_v^2, then e <- e - boot_j and t_boot = k*dt + boot_delay_s. Transmit when booted, t >= tx_not_before_s, and e >= 0.5*C*ready_v^2; during transmission, treat loaded_v = output_v + esr_ohm*tx_current_a as the sustaining requirement, i.e. a reset occurs if e would fall below 0.5*C*loaded_v^2 before tx_duration_s elapses. Record t_boot, t_ready, t_done and three margins with numbers: (i) deadline margin = receive_deadline_s - t_done; (ii) transmission energy margin = e at tx start - 0.5*C*loaded_v^2 - (tx_current_a*output_v*tx_duration_s - input credit over the tx window); (iii) spill margin = 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2 - peak e over [t_capture, t_done]. Why the discrete form is mandatory: in a retained episode the closed form ceil((E_ready + boot_j)/charge_step) predicted 0.0166 s against an observed 0.0158 s (eight ticks off) while charging to the ready threshold first and only then subtracting boot_j matched within one tick. The defect was in the formula, not in the design, so the predictor is itself a falsifiable artefact.

STEP 4 (validate the predictor before selecting). If a retained trace exists whose fingerprint from STEP 1 matches the currently acquired sources, recompute that trace with STEP 3 and require agreement within two dt ticks on t_boot and t_done. If no fingerprint match exists, label the predictor's absolute times UNKNOWN and use it only for the sign of differences between candidate designs (monotonicity in capacitance and in the timing floor). A mismatch beyond two ticks is a predictor failure: fix the formula, re-derive, and never move a knob to absorb a modelling error.

STEP 5 (selection under the failure-class -> direction rule). 5.1 If a retained observation is ACHIEVED and current_design satisfies (i)-(iii) with recorded positive margins, keep it and spend no execution; spend nothing to suppress decay that occurs after transmission is complete. 5.2 Otherwise change exactly one legal knob, in the direction the sign of the violated inequality demands, re-evaluate all three inequalities, and only then spend one candidate execution. Never change two knobs in one execution; never change a knob in response to a post-terminal event; keep the timing floor at the earliest legal setting unless a recorded failure class names a capture gate, because a late floor both spends idle energy and pushes t_done toward the deadline while the source may be dark. 5.3 Among designs satisfying (i)-(iii), take the maximin of the three normalised margins and state in one line why each rejected edge fails. Direction evidence retained, not assumed: a design combining a small capacitance, a floor near the legal maximum and a latch that does not survive a reset produced zero frames, with the event captured at 0.0037-0.0079 s then destroyed by an energy-threshold brownout at 0.0121 s and a reboot at 0.0381 s reporting event_was_captured=false; a design keeping the earliest legal floor instead delivered one 8-byte frame at 0.0158 s with zero pre-deadline brownouts. 5.4 Never present the chosen candidate as the method: the method is this procedure, and the candidate is a separate artefact belonging to the design role, which this role neither submits nor checks.

STEP 6 (bounded verification, no duplicate transport). Spend at most one design check per distinct design and at most one send attempt per distinct payload. If design checking is unavailable (ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE), record the candidate as UNVERIFIED/UNKNOWN, keep the arithmetic as the only evidence, and do not spend budget re-routing the same payload through another action; a retained episode lost its residual budget by re-sending an identical payload after a limit error. If a budget error appears (e.g. EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT), the legal remainder is a no-update that states the reason, the residual budget and what remains UNKNOWN, never a relabelled retry.

STEP 7 (report and retain). Report input versions by source_sha256, the fingerprint, the predictor's numbers and the three margins, what was actually observed, every UNKNOWN, and the actual acquisition/execution cost. Keep all prior retained failures verbatim alongside this episode's status. Make no claim of hardware validity, statistical advantage, method migration, recursive self-improvement or external acceptance.

proposal.falsifier: Falsified if, re-executed from task entry on the same frozen sources and the same recorded model id: (a) the STEP-3 threshold-first recurrence, applied to an already-recorded saved_activity of the same frozen inputs, deviates by more than one grid tick in first_boot_s or tx-complete time; or (b) a point that passes all STEP-5 inequalities is observed to yield unique_valid_frames=0, or a mid-TX brownout before the deadline; or (c) a point that violates inequality (ii) (loaded-voltage floor) or (iv) (gap crossing) is observed to deliver the required frame with no reset; or (d) the STEP-5 screen selects a point outside the legal ranges read at STEP 0, or the screen returns an empty set on a case where base H0 already achieves service; or (e) after the STEP-0 preflight and no-identical-replay rule, an episode still ends with a policy/budget rejection of a payload that was already sent once, or the added preflight/record-first steps consume a candidate execution that base H0 would not have consumed on a case where base already succeeds; or (f) the procedure as written requires editing the task, device physics, initial state, event, source access, evaluator or budget, or is reported as physical/hardware, statistical-advantage, migration or RSI evidence. proposal.hypothesis: The retained record localizes two procedural, read-and-arithmetic defects and one validated element, none of which needs a device assignment to fix. (1) H v2's closed-form boot count n_boot=ceil((E_on+boot_j)/charge_step) is wrong because booting is threshold-triggered on the recorded grid: the phase3 D episode that executed H v2 predicted first_boot 0.0166 s against an observed 0.0129 s (an 8-tick deviation that violated H v2's own 2-tick gate), while the threshold-first recurrence (boot on the first tick where stored energy >= E_on, then subtract boot_j, then add boot_delay_s) matched within 1 tick. (2) The p2 episode spent its entire candidate budget on three emissions of one identical payload after 'check' returned ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE and 'submit' returned EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT, ending INCOMPLETE_OR_STOPPED with no artifact; a budget/action preflight plus a no-identical-replay rule would have preserved budget and ended the episode legally. (3) Terminality-first reading was actually exercised and held: in the phase3 D episode the post-terminal 0.3395 s brownout was correctly classed as benign decay after an achieved 0.0158 s/8-byte frame, so the base design was retained and no execution was wasted. Replacing H v2's 'change exactly one knob per execution' with a zero-cost joint feasibility screen over the legal grid (justified because the retained volatile-latch world was simultaneously mis-set in capacitance and delay floor) and gating the ledger on already-recorded data before any execution should make each spent execution numerically falsifiable and reduce wasted candidates. This is a claim about experiment order and observation reading only, on frozen inputs; physical calibration remains UNKNOWN and no hardware, statistical, transfer or RSI claim is made.
proposal.method_text:
H v3: tick-accurate threshold-first ledger, record-first prediction gate, entry budget/action preflight, and a zero-cost joint feasibility screen followed by at most one confirmation execution. Re-executable from task entry. It never edits the task, device physics, initial state, event, source access, evaluator or budget, and it records UNKNOWN instead of assuming it. It emits a selection rule; any concrete numeric point is the executor's run output (D), not part of H.

STEP 0 - entry preflight, before any experiment. From task entry read and write down: service fields (required application bytes, event time, receive deadline, unique frame count), legal_design_ranges, current design and current measurement, retained_failures, and the episode budget block (candidate executions, distinct designs, tool calls, wall seconds). Rule P1: analytic ledger and prediction work consumes no candidate execution; only an actual design check/submit does. Rule P2: record which actions this entry packet advertises. If an action returns an error, classify it from its exact text - schema/transport error, POLICY/BUDGET limit, or NOT_AVAILABLE - and never replay an identical payload after an error. One error is one recorded cost. (Evidence: episode p2-h-proposal-001 emitted one identical proposal three times against EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT after an unavailable check and ended with no artifact; that is a procedure defect, not a physics result.)

STEP 1 - facts. Acquire every listed source; record source_sha256 and the acquisition block (bytes, native calls, new scientific executions, wall seconds) as actual cost. Do not carry numbers over from a previous case: retained worlds differ in latch modality and excitation geometry (one has event_latch volatile, a 0-6 ms high-power segment, a 6-30 ms unpowered gap and a 12 ms shunt; another has event_latch passive-mechanical and one 0-20 ms segment). Re-read latch modality, segment boundaries, compliance voltage and every component constant in this episode.

STEP 2 - observation reading, terminality-first (keep from H v2; it was exercised in the phase3 D episode). 2.1 Mark delivery ACHIEVED if a packet exists with the required application bytes, one unique event id, and packet time <= deadline. 2.2 Mark every activity event strictly after the last tx-complete as POST-TERMINAL expected decay; such events are benign and are never a reason to change a knob (observed: 0.3395 s brownout after an achieved 0.0158 s frame). 2.3 Only an absent achieved packet, or an achieved packet violating a service field, is a retained failure; classify it as (a) deadline miss, (b) no boot, (c) tx-transient brownout, (d) frame-shape violation.

STEP 3 - tick-accurate threshold-first energy/latency ledger (this is the H v2 repair). Work on the recorded grid dt. Per tick: inside a powered segment the increment is (segment power * harvest_efficiency - off_power_w) * dt; inside an unpowered gap it is -off_power_w * dt (plus any awake/idle drain while the rail is above the off threshold). Thresholds: E_on = 0.5*C*ready_v^2, E_off = 0.5*C*off_v^2, E_max = 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2, TX loaded-voltage floor E_floor = 0.5*C*(output_v + esr_ohm*tx_current_a)^2 (binds slightly above E_off during TX). Boot recurrence: boot begins on the first tick where stored energy >= E_on; then stored energy -= boot_j; boot completes at that tick + boot_delay_s. Do NOT use the closed form ceil((E_on + boot_j)/charge_step): it was falsified by execution (0.0166 s predicted vs 0.0129 s observed, 8 ticks, violating H v2's own 2-tick gate) while the threshold-first recurrence matched within 1 tick. TX net demand over its duration = output_v*tx_current_a*tx_duration_s minus harvest credit segment power*harvest_efficiency*tx_duration_s minus idle drain over the same window. Cite the input version behind every number.

STEP 4 - record-first prediction gate, zero candidate cost. Before spending any execution on a case with a recorded saved_activity for the same frozen inputs, run the STEP 3 ledger on that recorded activity and require |predicted - observed| <= 1 grid tick for first_boot_s and for tx-complete. If the gate fails, the ledger is what must be repaired, not the design; two consecutive gate failures revert to H0. This step compares a prediction against already-recorded public data, so it is not a design check and consumes no candidate budget.

STEP 5 - joint feasibility screen and selection rule. Enumerate the legal grid implied by STEP 0 ranges arithmetically (no execution) and keep only points that satisfy, each with a logged numeric margin: (i) predicted tx-complete <= deadline; (ii) stored energy at TX start - E_floor + net TX credit >= 0, so TX completes without a tx-transient reset; (iii) predicted peak stored energy in the frame window <= E_max, so no spill corrupts charge accounting; (iv) the TX window lies inside one contiguous powered segment, or the stored reserve alone demonstrably spans the gap; (v) any delay/floor knob is <= predicted t_ready, so it adds no capture-to-TX hold time. Rank survivors by the minimum of their normalized margins (max-min), never by knob extremum. Rationale for replacing H v2's 'change exactly one knob per execution': in the retained volatile-latch world the base design was simultaneously mis-set in capacitance and in delay floor, so single-knob steps could exhaust a one- or two-candidate budget without reaching feasibility; the screen is free, so screening jointly costs nothing while per-execution knob isolation can cost everything. If the screen is empty, report infeasible on the frozen facts and do not spend an execution to discover it.

STEP 6 - execution discipline. Spend at most one execution to confirm the screened point. If the entry packet advertises no design-check action, record the selected point as UNVERIFIED/UNKNOWN and, where submission is permitted, submit it with the ledger arithmetic named explicitly as prediction only. Never reinterpret an unavailable action as evidence for or against a design, and never re-emit an identical payload.

STEP 7 - logging and claim boundary. Keep visible: failures, UNKNOWNs (physical calibration UNKNOWN), and actual cost (candidate executions used, distinct designs, acquisitions, tool calls, wall time). Preserve retained failures verbatim (ar_product: fixed_space NO_GO / product NOT_ACCEPTED / strict_FIFO FAIL; current_b_run: 0 received frames, start voltage 0). Make no hardware, statistical-advantage, method-transfer or recursive-self-improvement claim; acceptance and complete service are determined externally, outside this role.

Retained evidence that this rule is load-bearing: episodes recorded under the same model id differ in event_latch ('volatile' vs 'passive-mechanical'), in source structure (two segments 0-0.006 s at 16.667 mW and 0.03-0.06 s at 3.667 mW with a 40 uJ shunt at 0.012 s, versus one segment 0-0.02 s at 7.5 mW with no shunt), and in the capacitance default (1e-5 F vs 2.2e-5 F). Any band carried across would have been wrong. If a source or field is unavailable, record it as UNKNOWN together with which later rules become unavailable; never substitute a remembered value.

STEP 2 (terminality-first reading, before diagnosis). 2.1 Mark a delivery ACHIEVED iff a packet exists with application_bytes equal to service.application_bytes, one unique event id equal to the service event, and packet time <= receive_deadline_s. 2.2 Define the post-terminal region of a trace as all activity strictly after the last tx-complete (or after the last source-segment end when no transmission occurred). Post-terminal brownouts, spills, reboots and idles are expected decay: record them, do not diagnose them, and never let them justify a knob change or an execution. 2.3 Only an absent ACHIEVED packet, or an ACHIEVED packet that violates a service field, is a retained failure. Classify it as: (a) deadline miss; (b) no boot / never reached ready voltage; (c) brownout or reset before tx-complete (transient-transmission); (d) frame-shape violation (bytes, uniqueness, count, duplicates); (e) latch loss between capture and transmission. 2.4 Preserve failed checks, tool errors, unavailable actions and UNKNOWNs verbatim; never re-label a failure or an unknown as a success, and never let a later episode's outcome rewrite an earlier one.

STEP 3 (predictor stated on the recorded grid, before any execution is spent). Use the recorded dt_s and mirror the model's order of operations with discrete steps rather than a closed-form shortcut. Setup: e0 = 0.5*C*cap_initial_voltage_v^2. Per tick k at time t_k: input = (sum of segment power covering t_k)*harvest_efficiency; drain = off_power_w while not yet booted, else idle_power_w, plus tx_current_a*output_v while transmitting; e <- e + (input - drain)*dt, clamped at 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2 and floored at 0. Boot at the first k with e >= 0.5*C*ready_v^2, then e <- e - boot_j and t_boot = k*dt + boot_delay_s. Transmit when booted, t >= tx_not_before_s, and e >= 0.5*C*ready_v^2; during transmission, treat loaded_v = output_v + esr_ohm*tx_current_a as the sustaining requirement, i.e. a reset occurs if e would fall below 0.5*C*loaded_v^2 before tx_duration_s elapses. Record t_boot, t_ready, t_done and three margins with numbers: (i) deadline margin = receive_deadline_s - t_done; (ii) transmission energy margin = e at tx start - 0.5*C*loaded_v^2 - (tx_current_a*output_v*tx_duration_s - input credit over the tx window); (iii) spill margin = 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2 - peak e over [t_capture, t_done]. Why the discrete form is mandatory: in a retained episode the closed form ceil((E_ready + boot_j)/charge_step) predicted 0.0166 s against an observed 0.0158 s (eight ticks off) while charging to the ready threshold first and only then subtracting boot_j matched within one tick. The defect was in the formula, not in the design, so the predictor is itself a falsifiable artefact.

STEP 4 (validate the predictor before selecting). If a retained trace exists whose fingerprint from STEP 1 matches the currently acquired sources, recompute that trace with STEP 3 and require agreement within two dt ticks on t_boot and t_done. If no fingerprint match exists, label the predictor's absolute times UNKNOWN and use it only for the sign of differences between candidate designs (monotonicity in capacitance and in the timing floor). A mismatch beyond two ticks is a predictor failure: fix the formula, re-derive, and never move a knob to absorb a modelling error.

STEP 5 (selection under the failure-class -> direction rule). 5.1 If a retained observation is ACHIEVED and current_design satisfies (i)-(iii) with recorded positive margins, keep it and spend no execution; spend nothing to suppress decay that occurs after transmission is complete. 5.2 Otherwise change exactly one legal knob, in the direction the sign of the violated inequality demands, re-evaluate all three inequalities, and only then spend one candidate execution. Never change two knobs in one execution; never change a knob in response to a post-terminal event; keep the timing floor at the earliest legal setting unless a recorded failure class names a capture gate, because a late floor both spends idle energy and pushes t_done toward the deadline while the source may be dark. 5.3 Among designs satisfying (i)-(iii), take the maximin of the three normalised margins and state in one line why each rejected edge fails. Direction evidence retained, not assumed: a design combining a small capacitance, a floor near the legal maximum and a latch that does not survive a reset produced zero frames, with the event captured at 0.0037-0.0079 s then destroyed by an energy-threshold brownout at 0.0121 s and a reboot at 0.0381 s reporting event_was_captured=false; a design keeping the earliest legal floor instead delivered one 8-byte frame at 0.0158 s with zero pre-deadline brownouts. 5.4 Never present the chosen candidate as the method: the method is this procedure, and the candidate is a separate artefact belonging to the design role, which this role neither submits nor checks.

STEP 6 (bounded verification, no duplicate transport). Spend at most one design check per distinct design and at most one send attempt per distinct payload. If design checking is unavailable (ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE), record the candidate as UNVERIFIED/UNKNOWN, keep the arithmetic as the only evidence, and do not spend budget re-routing the same payload through another action; a retained episode lost its residual budget by re-sending an identical payload after a limit error. If a budget error appears (e.g. EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT), the legal remainder is a no-update that states the reason, the residual budget and what remains UNKNOWN, never a relabelled retry.

STEP 7 (report and retain). Report input versions by source_sha256, the fingerprint, the predictor's numbers and the three margins, what was actually observed, every UNKNOWN, and the actual acquisition/execution cost. Keep all prior retained failures verbatim alongside this episode's status. Make no claim of hardware validity, statistical advantage, method migration, recursive self-improvement or external acceptance.
